s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cutaneous eruption with hyperkeratotic papules
salient_findings: Reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on the left leg
Slight bleeding after removal of scales
Compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate on biopsy
key_facts: 10-year history of slowly progressive cutaneous eruption
Asymptomatic
Location: front and back of the left leg from knee to ankle
Papules 1 to 10 mm wide
16-year history of diabetes mellitus
Treated with metformin
No history of another endocrine disorder or malignant neoplasm
No family history of similar cutaneous findings
Unremarkable hematological and biochemical test results
Lesional skin biopsy showed compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate in the superficial dermis is consistent with lichen planus

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic papules and epidermal atrophy are also seen in psoriasis, and the patient's 16-year history of diabetes mellitus may be relevant

shortlist.label: Lichenoid keratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Lesional skin biopsy showing compact hyperkeratosis and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate is also consistent with lichenoid keratosis

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological findings could also be consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus, although the lack of other systemic symptoms makes this less likely

shortlist.label: Granuloma faciale
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate and hyperkeratosis could also suggest granuloma faciale, although the location and morphology of the lesions are not typical
